title: Stabilization scripts and subscriber notice lab
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This page collects operator-focused stabilization scripts (checked, copy-paste ready commands and play sequences) plus a set of ‘subscriber notice’ templates intended for immediate use while a postmortem is prepared. The goal is to shorten mean time to customer-stable state (MTCS) by codifying low-risk, high-value remediation steps and pre-approved comms.

Scope and when to use this lab:
- Use for progressive degradations (elevated p95/p99 latency, token throttling, partial KV cache misses) and short outages (<6 hours).
- Not intended for full data-loss incidents or regulated-breach notifications (see Security incident process).

Quick decision ladder (operator):
1) Identify impact: who and what (API keys, routes, regions).
2) If impact is global or customer-critical, escalate to Incident Commander (IC) and open bridge.
3) Execute stabilization script matching the symptom class below.
4) Publish a subscriber notice (short status) within 15 minutes of bridge open.
5) Monitor metrics for 5–15 minutes; revert or escalate as needed.

Symptom classes and canonical stabilization scripts:
1) High tail latency (p95/p99) on generation routes:
   - Check autoscaling and queue depth:
     1. kubectl -n redwood get hpa --selector=app=runtime --output=wide
     2. curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/query?expr=queue_length{route=\"/v1/generate\"}"
   - If queues are backed and nodes are saturated: increase max pods (canary):
     1. kubectl -n redwood patch hpa runtime-gen -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10}}'
   - If scaling delayed, apply temporary rate-limit policy to non-critical routes:
     1. rwdctl routing set-rate --route /v1/embeddings --max-rps 50 --reason "protect-gen-p95"

2) KV cache miss storm (sharp rise in average tokens per request):
   - Flush LRU window for affected prefix group: rwdctl cache flush --prefix-prefix-group=default-llm-ops
   - Rotate to warm-only nodes: rwdctl runtime set-mode --pool warm-only --reason "cache-miss-mitigation"

3) Noisy neighbor/tenant causing GPU OOMs:
   - Identify offending tenant: curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/top-tenants?metric=gpu_ooms"
   - Throttle tenant: rwdctl quota update --tenant TENANT_ID --max-concurrency 2 --ttl 30m

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Pager 1 (oncall infra): system-level SLO misses, multi-service degradation.
- Pager 2 (runtime): sustained model errors, OOMs, severe latency after stabilization steps.
- Pager 3 (platform eng lead): customer-impacting degradation >30 minutes or customer escalations.

Subscriber notice templates (short, approved, fill-in fields):
1) Initial short notice (15 min):
Subject: [Status] Degraded responses for generation API in us-west-2
Body: We are aware of elevated latency impacting the generation API in us-west-2. Our on-call team has opened an investigation and applied initial mitigation steps. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Affected customers: developers using /v1/generate.

2) Update (after mitigation applied):
Subject: [Update] Mitigation in place for generation latency
Body: We have applied traffic shaping and scaled runtime capacity; error rates have fallen by ~70% and p95 latency is improving. We will continue to monitor and follow up with a root cause analysis within 48 hours. If you still see issues, reply to this message or contact support@redwood.example.

3) Post-incident follow-up (customer-facing RCA summary):
Subject: [Resolved] API latency incident — summary and next steps
Body: Incident period: 2026-01-12 14:18–16:02 UTC. Impact: elevated p95 latency for generation routes in us-west-2 affecting 12% of requests. Root cause: autoscaler backlog combined with an unbalanced sequence-length spike from a customer test. Actions taken: temporary scaling increase, rate-limits for non-critical routes, cache rotation. Next steps: autoscaler tuning, throttle-protection for heavy-sequence requests, and a postmortem scheduled for 72 hours.

Game-day lab (recommended exercises):
- Scenario A (15-minute stabilization): produce a synthetic 3x sequence-length spike to /v1/generate and exercise the stabilization script above. Verify RTO < 15 minutes and that an initial subscriber notice was posted automatically.
- Scenario B (noisy tenant): simulate tenant runaway job; exercise tenant throttling and verify fair-share metrics.
- Scenario C (partial region outage): disable a region and practice failover routing and status page messaging cadence.

Checklists and evidence to collect during incidents:
- Timestamps: bridge open, mitigation start, mitigation completion, first customer update, resolution.
- Key artifacts: pod logs (last 20k lines), stack traces, autoscaler events, observability queries used.
- Minimum evidence for postmortem: traffic profile, root cause hypothesis, mitigations applied, corrective actions and owner.

Post-incident actions and templates for the write-up:
1) Fill the short incident stub within 24 hours: title, impact, timeline, mitigations, owner for follow-ups.
2) Conduct memo-style postmortem within 72 hours with cross-functional reviewers.
3) Action items tracked in the incident backlog with owners and ETA.

Operational notes and safe-guards:
- All stabilization commands that change production config must be wrapped in a 30-minute automatic rollback unless explicitly extended by IC.
- Temporary rate limits should be documented in the incident bridge and removed when normal metrics return for 60 minutes.
- For any script that touches billing or quotas, notify Finance and Customer Success within 2 hours.

Appendix: quick observability queries and a status-page payload example:
- Observability queries (examples):
  - p95 latency: avg_over_time(latency_ms{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[5m])
  - queue depth: max(queue_length{route=\"/v1/generate\"})

- Status page incident payload (POST to statuspager.internal/incidents):
{
  "incident": {
    "status": "investigating",
    "component": "Generation API (us-west-2)",
    "impact": "degraded_performance",
    "message": "We are investigating elevated latency for some generation requests. Updates at 30min cadence."
  }
}

Ownership and contact list:
- Incident Commander rota: oncall-ic@redwood.example (primary), eng-leads@redwood.example (escalation).
- Runtime oncall: pager: +1-555-0102 (PagerDuty)

If you have suggestions to improve these scripts or templates, add a comment below or file an edit request against this page.
